title: Day-Count Conventions for Life-of-Tread Refunds
content:
**Life-of-Tread day count.** For a holder's cancellation of a Crestline Road Hazard Life-of-Tread Protection certificate refunded on the Life-of-Tread cancellation refund, the convention for the Life-of-Tread unused share turns on how long the certificate has been in force: the whole calendar months from the effective date to the cancellation date.

| Whole months from the effective date to the cancellation date | Life-of-Tread unused share |
|---|---|
| fewer than 12 | the actual days from the counting date to the expiration date, divided by the actual days from the effective date to the expiration date |
| at least 12 but fewer than 36 | the whole 30-day periods from the counting date to the expiration date, divided by the plan term in months (72 on the Life-of-Tread plan) |
| 36 or more | the whole calendar months from the counting date to the expiration date, divided by the plan term in months |

**Boundaries.** At 11 whole months in force the day convention applies; at exactly 12 the 30-day-period convention applies. At 35 whole months the 30-day-period convention applies; at exactly 36 the whole-month convention applies. Whole months are counted to the same day of the month; a partial month does not count toward the months in force.

**Hypothetical illustrations.**
- Day convention: 1,300 actual days from the counting date to expiration, in a term of 2,180 actual days, gives a share of 1,300 divided by 2,180.
- 30-day periods: 1,000 days to expiration contain 33 whole 30-day periods (990 days), so the share is 33 divided by 72.
- Whole months: 20 whole months to expiration give a share of 20 divided by 72.
